'Marvel's Wolverine' Comic Book Easter Eggs and References

Check out the comic art that inspired ‘Marvel’s Wolverine,’ available now on PlayStation 5 consoles.

BY Meagan Damore

Warning: This article might contain minor spoilers for Marvel’s Wolverine. 

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:41
Instaread

He ain’t no hero. He’s Wolverine. To be the best there is at what he does, Wolverine must also look the part, and so the creative team behind Marvel's Wolverine turned to the comics for inspiration. 

With more than 50 years of Logan to explore, Marvel's Wolverine draws references across all eras of the character's bloody history, from his earliest adventures to his brutal present. Here are just a few comics that inspired the game!

WOLVERINE (2003) #42

HEAR HIM ROAR! To give the character a proper introduction, Marvel's Wolverine turned to the WOLVERINE (2003) #42 cover by Humberto Ramos, which finds Logan in a fighting mood: claws out, crouched, and unleashing a furious roar.

MARVEL COMICS PRESENTS (1988) #81

GIVES IT TO YA! When Logan escaped the Weapon X facility in Barry Windsor-Smith's segment of MARVEL COMICS PRESENTS (1988) #81, he left a trail of bodies in his wake. Likewise, Marvel's Wolverine allows players to get just as vicious through the gameplay's combat mode.

X-MEN (1963) #509

GETTING TO THE POINT! Logan shares a turbulent, violent history with Lady Deathstrike that comes to a point in the final moments of Matt Fraction and Greg Land's X-MEN (1963) #509. The relationship between them doesn't improve much in Marvel's Wolverine, where an encounter ends with similar results.

WOLVERINE (1988) #10

FRIENDLY FIRE! One of Logan's first comic book encounters with Sabretooth, as depicted in Bill Sienkiewicz's cover to WOLVERINE (1988) #10, may be his last in Marvel's Wolverine. In a Marvel's Wolverine boss battle, Sabretooth strikes a similar pose while tussling with his frenemy Logan. 

WOLVERINE (1982) #2

NINJA ATTACK! During a trip to Japan in WOLVERINE (1982) #2, Logan finds himself in a scrap with a ninja clan that reaches a shattering conclusion. Marvel's Wolverine borrows a page from Chris Claremont and Frank Miller for a similar showdown. 

X-MEN (1963) #142

GOTTA HAND IT TO YOU! The John Byrne cover for X-MEN (1963) #142 gave Marvel's Wolverine the perfect fodder for Logan's Sentinel encounters. In both, Logan finds himself caught in the palm blast from a Sentinel, which ends in flame and fury for The Best There Is. 

X-MEN (2004) #178

IT AIN'T BRAIN SURGERY! In Marvel's Wolverine, Logan gets plenty of opportunity to prove he's the Best There Is against his Sentinel combatants. Fortunately, the comics provide plenty of references for that, including Salvador Larroca's iconic cover to X-MEN (2004) #178. 

Play Marvel's Wolverine on PlayStation 5 consoles now and find these comics and more on Marvel Unlimited!

Grab these comics and more at your local comic book shop! Or redeem your digital copy on the Marvel Unlimited app by using the code found in your print comic. Download the Marvel Unlimited app for iOS and Android devices today!

September 16's New Marvel Comics: The Full List

See the X-Men race to save humanity from forced evolution, watch the Avengers get torn apart, welcome Elektra back to Hell’s Kitchen, and more in this week's comics!

BY Meagan Damore

Evolution is contagious in this week's Marvel Comics!

The X-Virus is unleashed in DNX (2026) #1 by Jed MacKay and Federico Vicentini! The X-Men and 3K: each steered by an original heir of Xavier, each with their own vision for the mutant people—each at one another's throats. Cyclops and the Chairman both experienced the future of the Age of Revelation and came home with a renewed mission: the X-Men, to prevent that future; 3K, to own it. While the X-Men seek out the Fantastic Four to help save one of their own, the White Beast begins his plan to unleash the X-Virus in a major population area!

See the X-Men race to save humanity from forced evolution in DNX (2026) #1, on sale this Wednesday, September 16!

DNX spills over into Jed MacKay and Netho Diaz's X-MEN (2024) #37! While the X-Men battle 3K in a desperate bid to stave off disaster, Kid Omega engages in brain-to-brain combat with Cassandra Nova! It's the telepathic throwdown of the century!

Meanwhile, ARMAGEDDON continues in AVENGERS: ARMAGEDDON (2026) #4 by Chip Zdarsky, Frank Alpizar, and Delio Diaz Cespedes, which features a key moment in Marvel history as a new character takes the stage... The Marvel Universe changes forever right here and right now! The Avengers are torn apart as a shocking character makes their debut, setting the stage for November's AVENGERS #1!

Elsewhere, QUEEN IN BLACK rages on in Al Ewing, Iban Coello, and Paco Medina's QUEEN IN BLACK (2026) #4! As the war between Hela and Knull gets personal, Tyr unleashes his final weapon on the beleaguered Avengers! Meanwhile, in the Baxter Building, Reed Richards investigates Codex's half-symbiote power... with cataclysmic consequences! Will the end of Venom's golden era coincide with the end of Planet Earth?

Then, the Defenders have taken a beating on two fronts, emboldening Knull and Hela to personally finish off both strike teams once and for all in QUEEN IN BLACK: DEFENDERS OF LIGHT AND DARK (2026) #3 by Tom Waltz and Ze Carlos. The time has come for Plan B—but will this desperate contingency be enough for Team Light and Team Dark to stop the dual horrors of the Queen in Black and the God of Light from turning Planet Earth into yet another battlefield in their cosmic conflict? Light and Dark forces collide (and unite!) in this bombastic grand finale!

Additionally, Stephanie Phillips and Flaviano's DAREDEVIL (2026) #7 finds too many crooks in Hell's Kitchen! New York City is flooded... with crime! When an invaluable piece of evidence is out in the open, it's an all-out assault on the law from New York's most dangerous mobsters and murderers! But when old friend (and foe!) Elektra re-enters Matt Murdock's life after weeks apart, it could spell disaster for the Man Without Fear!

See the X-Men race to save humanity from forced evolution, watch the Avengers get torn apart, welcome Elektra back to Hell’s Kitchen, and more by picking up the latest titles this week! From fresh comics to collections and even Marvel Unlimited, find the full list of new releases here!

Essential Cookies

Always Active

Targeting & Advertising Cookies
